posts.name: AlexxKay
posts.cooked:
Cards under other cards (like Omni-Cannon) are considered in play (but have no text) unless the card on top says otherwise. For Omni-Cannon in particular, those cards are in play but they did not enter play (because of magic). When they get put under Omni-Cannon, “when a card enters play” triggers do not apply. They count when considering “the hero with the most cards in play.”

Do the cards under Savage Mana count towards Haka's "cards in play"?  Omni-Cannon cards obviously are Bunker's no matter how you look at it, but Savage Mana cards at least used to belong to other people.

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
AlexxKay:

Do the cards under Savage Mana count towards Haka's "cards in play"?  Omni-Cannon cards obviously are Bunker's no matter how you look at it, but Savage Mana cards at least used to belong to other people.

No, unless they happen to be cards from his deck (via Imbued Vitality). The cards remain "Baron Blade cards" or whatever deck they came from. They do not count toward Haka's cards in play, because they are not his.

Haka's cards under La Capitan would count towards his cards in play.

Note: for similar reasons, Infection and the Rod of Anubis do not count as cards in play for the hero they are next to.

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked: That's a weird one.  There's already a mechanism in place to handle what happens when a Limited card is put into play while a copy of it is already in play, so why layer on a restriction to the player's behavior to say that not only will it not work, you can't even attempt it.  Doesn't the fact that it won't work cover the thing we're worried about, i.e. having multiple copies of the Limited card in play?  I say, let 'em try it.  Won't work anyway.  Worst case, a player can try to seed their trash with extra copies of Limiteds they already have in play anyway.

posts.name: AlexxKay
posts.cooked: If Absolute Zero has a Modular Realignment in his hand, and is expecting some (partial) equipment destruction to come along soon, he could well want to dump a copy of a Limited-and-in-play card into his trash.  Whether he should be *able* to is, of course, a matter of opinion. But there's at least one legitimate use case.
